paper.title: Nearly Optimal Adaptive Procedure with Change Detection for Piecewise-Stationary Bandit

unmapped: Number of stationary segments M = S_T + 1; changes may be asynchronous across arms
Tuning (w, gamma) requires a lower bound on change amplitudes and minimum segment length (Assumption 1); Corollary 1 tuning of gamma uses M
settings.definition_quote: A piecewise-stationary bandit is characterized by a triple ... Assume that arm $k$'s reward at time $t$, $X_{k,t}$, is independently drawn from $f_{k,t}$ ... assume that the support of $f_{k,t}$ is a subset of $ [0,1]$ ... $\mathcal{R}(T) = \sum_{t=1}^T \max_{k} \mathbb{E}[X_{k,t}] - \mathbb{E}[\sum_{t=1}^T X_{A_t,t}]$.

symbols.D_c: sum_{i=1}^{M-1} min(w/2, ceil(b/delta^(i)) + 3 sqrt(w)), delta^(i) = max_k |mu_k^{i+1}-mu_k^i|

conditions: Assumption 1(a): M < floor(T/L) and nu_{i+1}-nu_i > L for all i, with L = w*ceil(K/gamma)
Assumption 1(b): at each change-point some arm has change amplitude >= 2 sqrt(log(2KT^2)/w) + 2 sqrt(log(2T)/w)
tuning: w and gamma chosen to satisfy Assumption 1

source.label: thm:bandit
source.quote: Running Algorithm~\ref{alg:bandit} with $w$ and $\gamma$ satisfying Assumption~\ref{assu0} and $b=[w\log(2KT^2)/2]^{1/2}$, we have \mathcal{R}(T) \leq \sum_{i=1}^M \tilde{C}_i +\gamma T + \sum_{i=1}^{M-1}\frac{2K \cdot \min(\frac{w}{2},\ceil{\frac{b}{\delta^{(i)}}}+3\sqrt{w})}{\gamma}+3M ...

results.notes: Regret is measured against the per-round best arm (via means), i.e. dynamic regret; the per-round best sequence has at most M-1 switches.

symbols.delta_ch: known lower bound on min_i max_k delta_k^(i) (change amplitude)

conditions: delta_ch > 0 is a lower bound on min_i max_k delta_k^(i)
Assumption 1 (inherited from Theorem 1): segments longer than L = w ceil(K/gamma), M < floor(T/L), change amplitudes above threshold
tuning: gamma = sqrt((M-1) K min(w/2, ceil(b/delta)+3 sqrt(w))/(2T))

source.label: corr:regret
source.quote: Assume $\delta>0$ is a lower bound on $\min_i \max_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \delta_k^{(i)}$. If we run Algorithm~\ref{alg:bandit} with a window-length $w$, $b=[w\log(2KT^2)/2]^{1/2}$, and $\gamma = \sqrt{(M-1) K\cdot\min(w/2,\ceil{b/\delta}+3\sqrt{w})/(2T)}$, then we have \mathcal{R}(T) \leq \sum_{i=1}^M \tilde{C}_i + 4 \sqrt{ (M-1) TK\cdot \min(w/2,\ceil{b/\delta}+3\sqrt{w})}+3M.

results.notes: Corollary's gamma requires knowledge of M. Paper informally states this is O(sqrt(MKT log T)) for fixed w; Assumption 1 inheritance is implicit.
